$comment: The signal-name-hyphen issues of a Kotlin file: names (the quoted name each is on), fixes (the replacement texts of each), messages, severities, and fixed (the file with every fix applied). Read by SignalNameHyphensTest.kt and signalNameHyphens.test.ts.

cases.name: a hyphen in each place that names a signal is an error with the camelCase fix
cases.src:
import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.html.*
fun page() = div {
  dataSignals("foo-bar", "1")
  dataSignals("count" to 0, "user-name" to "")
  dataComputed("full-name", "1")
  dataBind("form.first-name")
  dataRef("my-ref")
  dataIndicator("is-busy")
  dataMatchMedia("is-dark", "(prefers-color-scheme: dark)")
  dataText(signal("form.first-name"))
  dataOnClick(statements(increment("click-count"), toggle("is-open"), set("a-b", 1)))
}
suspend fun send(stream: DatastarStream) {
  stream.patchSignals("foo-bar" to 1, "ok" to 2)
  stream.removeSignals("ok", "foo-bar")
}

cases.name: a key with a hyphen that is data is left alone
cases.src:
import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.html.*
fun page() = div {
  dataSignals("user" to mapOf("first-name" to ""))
  dataSignals("{'foo-bar': 1}")
  dataSignals("{'foo-bar': 1}", true)
  dataComputed("{'full-name': () => 1}")
  dataText(signal("user['first-name']"))
  dataOn("my-event", "x()")
  dataClass("is-open", "true")
}
suspend fun send(stream: DatastarStream) {
  stream.patchSignals("user" to mapOf("first-name" to null))
  stream.patchSignals("""{"foo-bar": 1}""")
}

cases.name: a name that may not be a signal's is left alone
the fix and the bracket form leave a key inside brackets as it is
cases.src:
import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.html.*
fun p() = div { dataText(signal("form.first-name['x-y']")); dataText(signal("items[0]-x")); dataText(signal("a-b.c-d")) }
messages: A signal name holds no hyphen: Datastar's client reads one as a capital in an attribute key and as a hyphen in an expression or a patch, so Streamlord refuses "form.first-name['x-y']" at runtime. Write form.firstName['x-y'].

A signal name holds no hyphen: Datastar's client reads one as a capital in an attribute key and as a hyphen in an expression or a patch, so Streamlord refuses "items[0]-x" at runtime. Write items[0]X.
A signal name holds no hyphen: Datastar's client reads one as a capital in an attribute key and as a hyphen in an expression or a patch, so Streamlord refuses "a-b.c-d" at runtime. Write aB.cD.

cases.name: a name is read as the client reads it
messages: A signal name holds no hyphen: Datastar's client reads one as a capital in an attribute key and as a hyphen in an expression or a patch, so Streamlord refuses "items[\$i-1]" at runtime. It looks like a subtraction, which belongs in the expression: \$items[\$i - 1].

A signal name holds no hyphen: Datastar's client reads one as a capital in an attribute key and as a hyphen in an expression or a patch, so Streamlord refuses "a['['].b-c" at runtime. Write a['['].bC.

cases.name: a call inside a string template is read, and a templated name is reported without a fix
cases.src:
import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.html.*
import kotlin.collections.set
fun p(id: Int, expr: String) = div {
  dataText("${signal("is-running")} ? 'Stop' : 'Go'")
  dataOnClick("${set("click-count", 1)}; @post('/x')")
  dataSignals("item-$id" to false)
  dataComputed("full-name", expr)
  dataOnClick(setExpr("draft-text", "''"))
}
messages: A signal name holds no hyphen: Datastar's client reads one as a capital in an attribute key and as a hyphen in an expression or a patch, so Streamlord refuses "is-running" at runtime. Write isRunning, or ['is-running'] for a key with a hyphen in it.

A signal name holds no hyphen: Datastar's client reads one as a capital in an attribute key and as a hyphen in an expression or a patch, so Streamlord refuses "click-count" at runtime. Write clickCount, or ['click-count'] for a key with a hyphen in it.

A signal name holds no hyphen: Datastar's client reads one as a capital in an attribute key and as a hyphen in an expression or a patch, so Streamlord refuses "item-$id" at runtime. Write it in camelCase.
A signal name holds no hyphen: Datastar's client reads one as a capital in an attribute key and as a hyphen in an expression or a patch, so Streamlord refuses "full-name" at runtime. Write fullName.

A signal name holds no hyphen: Datastar's client reads one as a capital in an attribute key and as a hyphen in an expression or a patch, so Streamlord refuses "draft-text" at runtime. Write draftText, or ['draft-text'] for a key with a hyphen in it.
